'''C. J. McCollum''' (born September 19, 1991) is an American college basketball player.  He is currently a senior at [[Lehigh University]] majoring in Journalism and was the [[Patriot League Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] in both 2010 and 2012.

McCollum, a 6'3" guard from [[GlenOak High School]] in [[Canton, Ohio]], came to Lehigh is 2009 and made an instant impact.  In his freshman year, McCollum averaged 19.1 points and 5.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game.  He made [[Patriot League]] history as he was the first freshman to be named conference player of the year<ref>[http://www.patriotleague.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030110aaa.html Patriot League Men's Basketball All-League Teams and Awards Announced], accessed November 14, 2011</ref> and was also named an [[Associated Press|AP]] honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].  He led the Mountain Hawks to the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010 NCAA Tournament]], where he scored 26 points in a first round loss to top seed Kansas.<ref name=BIO>[http://www.lehighsports.com/sports/mbball/rosters/displayplayer.aspx?playerid=8006 Lehigh athletics biography], accessed November 14, 2011</ref>

As a sophomore, McCollum upped his averages to 21.8 points and 7.8 rebounds per game.  However, his shooting percentages and Lehigh's record slipped and McCollum was beaten out for conference player of the year honors by [[Bucknell Bison men's basketball|Bucknell's]] [[Mike Muscala]].  He was named first team All-Conference.<ref name=BIO/>

As a junior, McCollum was again named Patriot League player of the year and earned his third straight first team all-conference designation.<ref>{{Cite web | title = 2011-12 Men's Basketball All-Patriot League Teams and Major Awards Announced | publisher = [[Patriot League]] | date = 27 February 2012 | url = http://www.patriotleague.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022712aaa.html | format = Press release | accessdate = 27 February 2012}}</ref>

In the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]], he scored 30 points as Lehigh won its first-round game against the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] by 75-70, making it only the sixth time that a 15th seed has defeated a 2nd seed and the second of the night.<ref name="morningcall">{{cite web | url=http://www.mcall.com/sports/college/lehigh/mc-ncaa-basketball-lehigh-duke-gamer-0316-20120316,0,6364456.story | title=NCAA basketball: Lehigh pulls off monumental upset of Duke | publisher=The Morning Call | work=MCall.com | date=March 16, 2012 | accessdate=March 16, 2012 | author=Housenick, Tom}}</ref>

Considered a top NBA draft prospect in his junior year, he explained his reasons for continuing his education at Lehigh in an article that he wrote himself for [[The Sporting News]]  [http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-04-09/cj-mccollum-lehigh-nba-draft-staying]

On November 25, 2012, McCollum scored 26 points in a 91–77 win over [[Sacred Heart Pioneers men's basketball|Sacred Heart]], which made him surpass [[Rob Feaster]] as the [[Patriot League]]'s all-time leading scorer.<ref>{{Cite web |title =McCollum breaks record in 91–77 win at Sacred Heart | work =Sports | publisher = [[Lehigh University]]| date =25 November 2012| url = http://www.lehighsports.com/sports/mbball/mccollum_breaks_record_in_91-77_win_at_sacred_heart.aspx| accessdate = 26 November 2012}}</ref> On January 5, 2013, McCollum broke his left foot in a game versus [[VCU Rams men's basketball|Virginia Commonwealth University]], ending his season. He was a 2012–13 [[List of Senior CLASS Award men's basketball winners|Senior CLASS Award]] finalist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020613aad.html|title=Hulls Named Finalist for Senior CLASS Award|accessdate=2013-02-13|date=2013-02-06|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=IUHoosiers.com}}</ref>

Despite his injury ending his career with Lehigh, McCollum is expected to be the first Lehigh player to ever be drafted in the NBA, and the first to be invited to the NBA's green room.
